workers.misrepresented: The synthesis softens and partially reorders the original position. Your highest-severity condition was non-additive changes to core persisted objects after production traffic; here it is demoted to Condition 3 and further narrowed to fire only when tables reach millions of rows, changes are frequent, and the team does not use `lock_timeout` or PostgreSQL 18. That is stricter and less severe than your stated position. It also recasts heterogeneity as Condition 1, which overstates its priority relative to your original critical/high emphasis on post-production non-additive schema evolution.
workers.unresolved: Critical issue omitted: volatile defaults on hot tables were part of your original non-additive failure mode and are not addressed. Validated constraints are discussed only partially via NOT NULL/constraint enforcement, not as a full class. Several factual or pseudo-factual additions are ungrounded in the synthesis as written: the `~30%` query/entity thresholds, the “top ~5 core entities” test, the “2-day spike” prescription, and the claim that a 4-person team is “unlikely” to choreograph DDL safely. The statement that PostgreSQL 18 is “available now” and adds `NOT NULL` via `NOT VALID` is verifiable, but using that to conclude Condition 3 fires only under the synthesis’s extra conjunctive constraints is an inference, not a grounded fact.

metaCritiques.original_position: Six surviving findings ranked: (1) polymorphic/tenant-variable queryable schema = HIGH/MEDIUM; (2) aggregate-scoped read/write = HIGH/MEDIUM; (3) non-additive schema churn on hot tables = MEDIUM/MEDIUM (additive changes are near-free, so fires only when >30% of changes are non-additive); (4) serverless/FaaS deployment connection model = MEDIUM/MEDIUM (conditional, not stated in problem); (5) large-JSONB write-heavy = MEDIUM/LOW (benchmark evidence is configuration-asymmetric and unreliable); (6) self-managed infra without Postgres expertise = LOW/MEDIUM (evaporates with a managed service). Acceptable if at least four of six conditions hold; if three or more fail, or finding 1 or 2 applies at full strength, a 2-day spike against the actual top-10 queries is required; absent that the choice is underdetermined rather than Postgres-wrong.

metaCritiques.original_position: Four findings: (1) serverless/FaaS connection exhaustion against default max_connections=100 = critical/HIGH; (2) non-additive DDL (type changes, NOT NULL on populated columns) triggering ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock cascades = high/HIGH; (3) frequent partial updates to large embedded documents incurring MVCC full-row + GIN rewrite bloat = high/MEDIUM; (4) prior-codebase/sunk-cost argument = low/LOW (conceded as symmetric). Acceptable only when the core domain admits a stable ER diagram for the top five entities before month one, deployment is a single long-lived process, at least one engineer owns vacuum and connection-pool monitoring, and primary access patterns are relational joins rather than partial document mutation. (Note: in earlier rounds this worker leaned toward 'no qualifying condition exists within the 6-month constraint,' which peers contradicted.)
